comparator.name: Food Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026 study handbook defines a 150-EC common part and 30 EC free-choice space. The common part comprises a 123-EC compulsory credited cluster, one 3-EC restricted-choice mathematics course and a compulsory 24-EC BSc thesis. Mathematics Applied: Introduction is selected from the two published 3-EC mathematics options by official order. General Safety and Laboratory Safety are zero-credit requirements and are not counted as EC-bearing components. The programme has no formal specialization route; the programme page's examples of minors describe ways to use the free-choice space rather than mutually exclusive degree routes. Independent UCR reassessment on 2026-10-17 preserves the settled full 180-EC reconstruction and generic route. The current official programme page and linked October 2026 course diagram corroborate the chemistry, physics, microbiology, food-processing, product-quality and thesis structure. The current page explicitly names Foods of Animal Origin and Psychobiology of Eating Behaviour as possible minors, not compulsory specializations. The interactive study handbook was inaccessible during this review; its previously verified EC weights and neutral mathematics choice are retained rather than reconstructed again from a recruitment diagram.
components: First-listed option in the 3-EC restricted-choice mathematics group.
BSc Thesis Food Science and Technology
Compulsory bachelor thesis in the common part.
Genuine free-choice space; no specific minor or elective package is assumed.

core: Molecular and biochemical foundations of food ingredients and biological production
Food microbiology, safety, hazards and effects on health
Food-product development, processing, preservation, packaging and quality
Mathematics, statistics, laboratory investigation and independent food research
Nutrition, digestion, perception and health in relation to food
Sustainable production, plant-based innovation, protein transition and circular product systems
adjacent: Psychobiology of eating behaviour and consumer responses to food
Sustainable food systems, agricultural production and environmental resources
Foods of animal origin as an optional minor direction
questions: How can molecular science, product research and circular resource use inform sustainable food innovation?
How do physiology, cognition, health behaviour and consumer research help explain eating choices?
How can agricultural systems meet food needs while reducing environmental harm?

candidates.label: Eating behaviour, health and consumer research
Ecological and governance approaches to sustainable food systems

alternatives.label: Biochemistry, circular production & product development
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines seven life/health-science courses, eight environmental/sustainability courses, three product/enterprise courses and five quantitative-method courses, plus mandatory PPD. The label gives the molecular, circular-production and product-development strands appropriate joint emphasis; it does not call the programme Food Technology.
alternatives.concept: Combine cell biology, biochemistry, microbial laboratory methods and physiology with product design, consumer research and quantitative investigation. Farming, lifecycle analysis, resource recovery and environmental governance connect biological production to circular product systems. This provides a related route into sustainable food-product questions; it does not supply the cumulative food-chemistry, food-physics, preservation or process-engineering curriculum.
progression: Exact planned availability and formal prerequisites pass against the current workbook. Research Methods precedes multivariate statistics; biological and sustainability gateways precede their dependent courses. Where relevant, ecology precedes farming, biodiversity precedes conservation, and foundational economics precedes advanced economics. Data handling and introductory methods precede final-year empirical or evidence-synthesis work.

alternatives.label: Health, eating behaviour & consumer research
alternatives.labelReason: Psychology, cognition and physiology provide the explanatory core, while consumer research, product development, behavioural economics and methods give substantial additional study. Eating behaviour is the evidenced application of these courses, not a claim that each is food-specific.
alternatives.concept: Investigate eating choices through physiological and biochemical foundations, brain function, perception, social psychology and health behaviour. Consumer research, product design, behavioural economics and communication connect these mechanisms to product acceptance and health messages. The courses provide general scientific and research tools for this application, rather than a specialist nutrition, sensory-food-science or food-processing sequence.
progression: Exact planned availability and formal prerequisites pass against the current workbook. Research Methods precedes multivariate statistics; biological and sustainability gateways precede their dependent courses. Where relevant, ecology precedes farming, biodiversity precedes conservation, and foundational economics precedes advanced economics. Data handling and introductory methods precede final-year empirical or evidence-synthesis work.
alternatives.distinctness: Thirteen courses / 97.5 EC differ from the first programme in each direction. The molecular/laboratory and circular-production sequence gives way to brain function, perception, psychology, lifespan development, behavioural economics, marketing, persuasion and qualitative inquiry. This changes the organising question from biological production and circular products to eating behaviour and consumer responses.
traceOverrides: teaches consumer needs assessment, prototypes and product development, supplying a transferable method to connect eating-behaviour research with product design; food-specific product science is absent
teaches population-health patterns, disease risks and evaluation of evidence, supplying a specific method to assess health-related eating behaviour without claiming specialist nutrition teaching

alternatives.label: Ecology, circular resources & sustainable food systems
alternatives.labelReason: Environmental, ecological and resource courses dominate the schedule; economics, methods, ethics and product design connect that science to sustainable production. Food systems is the evidenced application, with Sustainable Farming and food-governance problems providing explicit curricular anchors.
alternatives.concept: Apply ecology, soil and water science, lifecycle analysis and circular-resource methods to the environmental conditions of food production. Sustainable farming, environmental governance, economics and product design connect agricultural practices to resource use and collective choices. Most courses teach transferable environmental mechanisms and methods; this is a food-systems application rather than a food-manufacturing or food-engineering degree.
progression: Exact planned availability and formal prerequisites pass against the current workbook. Research Methods precedes multivariate statistics; biological and sustainability gateways precede their dependent courses. Where relevant, ecology precedes farming, biodiversity precedes conservation, and foundational economics precedes advanced economics. Data handling and introductory methods precede final-year empirical or evidence-synthesis work.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten courses / 75 EC differ from the first programme and eighteen / 135 EC from the second. Biodiversity, conservation, climate change, soil/water science, Earth observation, renewable systems and economics replace molecular/laboratory or psychological specialisation. This shifts the unit of analysis from ingredients/products or eating behaviour to agricultural ecosystems, environmental resources and governance.
traceOverrides: teaches product lifecycle, material choices, industrial production and environmental impact, supplying a concrete complementary method to assess circular products within sustainable food systems
teaches cellular energy, genetics and biological communication as the biological foundation for analysing organisms and production in agroecosystems

selection.assessment: Three coherent programmes were included sequentially. Product-science, plant-based/protein-transition and sustainable-packaging interests are represented within the first integrated concept, with food-specific chemical and engineering gaps explicit. The eating-behaviour minor supports the distinct second curriculum; the sustainable-food-systems interest supports the third. The animal-origin minor was assessed individually: biodiversity, physiology, biochemistry and laboratory methods provide biological foundations, but there is no animal-food production, dairy/meat science, animal-food microbiology or processing sequence sufficient for a complete independent 24-course direction. General biology cannot be relabelled as Foods of Animal Origin. All three accepted responses are related academic programmes, not substitutes for Food Technology.

notes.text: Wageningen Food Technology provides a cumulative food-science and engineering curriculum, including food chemistry, microbiology, physics, preservation, processing, packaging and quality. These UCR programmes approach related questions through molecular and environmental science, eating behaviour and consumer research, or sustainable food systems. They do not reproduce that specialist food-technology sequence.
